approach:
Route by the presence of the five-field brief, in code, in three places that must agree: steward.rs decide(), work_decisions.rs open_proposals/in_limit, and the owner decisions page (xtask/src/decisions.rs needs_owner). A change with a brief is owner-bound at any rung: decide() never applies it, records it as Decision::Proposed with kind Proposal and the brief. A change without a brief is applied if role.may_change(rung); otherwise it is recorded with brief None and reaches no owner surface. open_proposals lists an undecided proposal when it has a brief, or has none and the raising role may change its rung (the drain approves those; the audience role's items rely on that). in_limit is false for a briefed item, so the drain never auto-approves an owner-bound item. A new constructor, blind_spot_needing_owner, gives a missing-token blind spot a brief, kind Proposal, a distinct key, and evidence (the source), so WorkItem::validate passes (round-1 blocker). validate_items passes a blind spot's checked brief to it and requires a request for an in-limit rung only when there is no brief. STEWARD_PROMPT is rewritten inside the 600-token budget: step back across repeated failures and blind spots, decide and queue a request itself, write a brief only for an environment change or a token or credential, and put the owner's action in if_yes. The role goes to version 3. The docs, CHANGELOG and decision D169 mark the prompt rule prose-only and the routing code-enforced.

Changes since round 1: the blocker (evidence on the briefed blind spot) is fixed and tested through steward::run; the decisions page is brought into line; the silent-key risk is stated and documented; the owner action for a token goes in if_yes.

decisions.choice: A brief present means owner-bound at any rung. decide() skips the apply step, returns Decision::Proposed, keeps the brief, and sets kind Proposal when a brief is present.
decisions.reason: Base decide() (steward.rs:701-712) applies in-limit changes and drops their brief, so an env/token need at implementation (a missing GH_TOKEN) never reached the owner. open_proposals and find_open (work_decisions.rs:47, 93) handle only kind Proposal, so a briefed repeated-failure or blind-spot item must become Proposal to be seen.

rejected.option: Keep applying in-limit changes and attach the brief only above the limit (base behavior).
rejected.why: This is the fault: env/token needs are hidden, and above-limit changes without a brief reach the owner.

rejected.option: Add a code check that refuses briefs for anything but env/token needs.
rejected.why: Out of scope. The prompt limits briefs (prose-only); code routes by brief presence.

decisions.choice: Round-1 blocker (finding 3): blind_spot_needing_owner(source, title, brief) builds a ProposedChange with kind Proposal, rung Implementation, source Reference::path(source), evidence vec![Reference::path(source)], the blind_spot_request text, and brief Some. Its key is blind_spot_key(source) + ':owner-action', for example blind-spot:github:owner-action. decide() sets kind Proposal for any briefed change. blind_spot_change is unchanged.
decisions.reason: WorkItem::validate (records/work.rs:131) refuses a non-BlindSpot item with empty evidence, and run() calls item.validate() for every decided item (steward.rs:1328), so a briefed blind spot with empty evidence would fail the whole run and commit nothing. Evidence fixes that. The distinct key stops a plain blind-spot:github item recorded earlier (a transient gh error, already in known_keys, steward.rs:1286) from silently swallowing a later token need. approve_request on the source path only prints 'This path is not in the repository' (work_decisions.rs:221-223), so the extra evidence is harmless.

rejected.option: Keep kind BlindSpot and make open_proposals, find_open and xtask read_snapshot accept any undecided item with a brief.
rejected.why: It changes three readers (core, status, xtask) and the kind filter at work_decisions.rs:47, 93 and xtask/src/decisions.rs:286, for one case. Giving the item evidence and kind Proposal changes one constructor.

rejected.option: Reuse blind_spot_key unchanged for the briefed variant.
rejected.why: A plain blind spot for the same source recorded earlier would block the briefed one through the seen-key set (steward.rs:1322-1325).

decisions.choice: open_proposals keeps an undecided Proposal when brief.is_some() || in_limit(records, item); in_limit gains brief.is_none() &&; split_open is unchanged (briefed goes to 'above', unbriefed in-limit to 'within').
decisions.reason: Unbriefed above-limit proposals must not be listed (criterion 1). The audience role raises unbriefed Implementation proposals that its own test expects in status.work_proposals (crates/athena-cli/tests/audience.rs:149). That role is recorded with limit Implementation in the same commit, so they are in limit and the drain approves them. Both criteria hold and the audience role is untouched.

rejected.option: List only items with a brief.
rejected.why: It hides the audience role's in-limit items from athena status and from the drain, and the audience role is out of scope.
split_open partitions open_proposals by in_limit, so the new in_limit gives the right split.

decisions.choice: Finding 4: needs_owner in xtask/src/decisions.rs becomes item.brief.is_some(), and the page tests are updated. xtask/src/decisions.rs is added as a needed file.
decisions.reason: The page is the owner's decisions surface. Routing by rung there would hide env/token briefs at implementation and keep showing unbriefed above-limit items as 'No brief written yet', the same fault in a third place. The change is one function plus fixtures. A proposal the owner has not been told to decide stays reachable by id (approve-work, reject-work) and in the records.

rejected.option: Leave xtask out and document that the page does not show env/token briefs.
rejected.why: The owner would never see the item on the page they judge by; docs and CHANGELOG would have to say the routing is incomplete.

decisions.choice: Finding 5: no change to the seen-key rule. An unbriefed above-limit item is recorded and then visible only in the records (and by id). Its key stays in known_keys, so the steward does not raise it again. This is a stated risk, and docs/design/roles-and-ladder.md and D169 say where such items can be seen.
decisions.reason: Dropping their keys from seen would make the steward record the same finding again on every run, since nothing marks it decided. A model that later finds an env/token need writes a new key, or for a blind spot the distinct :owner-action key.

rejected.option: Leave unbriefed undecided above-limit keys out of the seen set.
rejected.why: It creates a fresh duplicate work item every run.

decisions.choice: Finding 6: the owner's action goes in the brief's if_yes. The prompt says 'put what the owner must do in if_yes' and the brief() user prompt says a missing GH_TOKEN or GITHUB_TOKEN is a github blind spot whose if_yes names setting it. The docs say approve-work is used only after the owner has supplied the token or made the environment change.
decisions.reason: A producer job cannot set an environment variable. The brief text is what tells the owner the action; approve-work queues the make-readable job, which is useful only after the token is in place.

rejected.option: Make approve-work check that the token is set.
rejected.why: New code outside scope; the steward cannot see the model's gh environment (the token passing lives in athena-agent env.rs).

decisions.choice: validate_items requires a request for an in-limit rung only when the item has no brief; a briefed blind-spot item goes through check_brief and then blind_spot_needing_owner.
decisions.reason: A briefed item is never applied, so a request is dead text; the check at steward.rs:961 would otherwise drop an owner-bound item at implementation. The output schema already has an optional brief on every item (outputs.rs:322), so the schema is unchanged.

rejected.option: Keep requiring a request for every in-limit item.
rejected.why: It forces dead text or drops the owner-bound item.
The steward process cannot see the model's gh environment.

decisions.choice: Keep two Decision variants. Decision::Proposed means 'not applied, work item recorded'. Whether the owner sees it depends on the item's brief.
decisions.reason: A third variant would touch run() and every match for no behavior gain; the item's brief is the measured signal.

rejected.why: More churn in run() and tests; the owner-visible fact is the brief.

decisions.choice: The prompt fits by rewriting STEWARD_PROMPT in fewer bytes (about 868 or fewer for prompt text, the contract being 929 bytes, D168). Role version 3. The new context test measures the real composed set.
decisions.reason: Budgets never rise to fit a set (lib.rs:176-178). The base context test composes only a placeholder, so the real prompt was never measured.

risks.risk: The new prompt does not fit: the composed steward set is limited to 1800 bytes (600 tokens × 3), the contract takes 929 plus separators, so the prompt text is about 868 bytes or less, and the current one leaves only about 150 bytes of room.
risks.mitigation: Step 1 writes the prompt and step 2 measures it with the new context test before anything else. Required terms are fixed by the roles.rs tests (question, if_yes, if_no, cost, recommendation, one-line reason, short, plain, no jargon, step back, repeated failures, blind spots, decide, request, environment, token, credential, owner action in if_yes). Drop prose that restates the schema first. The budget is never raised.

risks.risk: The model writes a brief for a non-env/token item, or omits one for a real token need. Code does not check the reason (out of scope).
risks.mitigation: The prompt wording is marked prose-only in the docs. The routing holds either way: a brief reaches the owner, no brief never does. The measured check is the item's brief and open_proposals.

risks.risk: Finding 5: an unbriefed above-limit item is recorded and then seen by no one except in the records or by id, and its key (in known_keys) stops the steward raising it again.
risks.mitigation: Stated in the docs and D169: such items are visible in the records branch and decidable by id only. If the finding later turns into an env/token need, the model uses a new key; for a blind spot the :owner-action key is distinct. Dropping the keys from the seen set was rejected because it would create a duplicate work item every run.

risks.risk: A within-limit unbriefed steward item of kind Proposal that was applied (a request already queued) stays open, so the drain could approve it a second time. This exists at base: nothing records a decision for an applied item.
risks.mitigation: Not changed here. decide() still applies only when there is no brief, and the prompt says proposals are for rungs above the limit. Listed so the next change can close it.

risks.risk: Role version 3 means the next steward run commits a new role record; a store with only version 2 recorded shows an extra role record.
risks.mitigation: This is the designed path (role_recorded check, run() lines 1345-1349); role_limit takes the newest version, so the limit does not change.

risks.risk: A briefed blind spot recorded as kind Proposal could fail WorkItem::validate (round-1 blocker).
risks.mitigation: blind_spot_needing_owner sets evidence to the source reference, and the new end-to-end test runs steward::run on a briefed github blind spot and asserts the run succeeds and the commit holds the item. A core test also runs decide() then item.validate().

demonstrations.method: Unit tests in steward.rs mod tests and work_decisions.rs mod tests. In steward.rs, a new plain_change(rung) helper (brief None) at DesignDecisions, BriefRequirements and OwnerGoals goes through decide() with the Counting applier. In work_decisions.rs, the resulting item (kind Proposal, role steward, steward role recorded in Records, no decision) is put in a Records and passed to open_proposals and split_open.
demonstrations.observes: Decision::Proposed, the applier is called zero times, item.brief is None, and open_proposals(&records) is empty. A briefed copy of the same item is listed alone, and split_open puts it in 'above'. An unbriefed in-limit item still goes to 'within'. An unbriefed item from a role with no recorded definition is not listed.
demonstrations.fails_without: With the base open_proposals (work_decisions.rs:43-51) every undecided Proposal is listed, so the 'not listed' assertion fails. With the base decide(), a non-brief change keeps change.brief, which is how the rejected job leaked briefless proposals.
demonstrations.seam: Entry points: steward::decide(role, change, applier, taken, now) and work_decisions::open_proposals(&Records). Fakes: the Counting applier passed as &dyn Applier (exists, steward.rs tests) and a Records::default() filled with roles::steward(at()) and the work item, as in the work_decisions.rs tests (exists). The plan_change helper and the new tests are added by steps 5 and 6.

demonstrations.method: Core: a briefed change at each of the five rungs (including Implementation and DefaultsConventions) goes through decide(): Decision::Proposed, zero applier calls, item.brief equal to the brief, kind Proposal, item.validate() Ok, listed by open_proposals. A blind_spot_needing_owner('github', ..., GH_TOKEN brief) goes through decide() and item.validate() is Ok. validate_items accepts a briefed in-limit item with no request and a github blind spot with a brief, and still refuses an unbriefed in-limit item with no request. End to end, in crates/athena-cli/tests/steward.rs: a_missing_token_reaches_the_owner_with_its_brief_and_a_plain_gap_does_not scripts the fake steward (steward_scenario) to report (1) a blind-spot item for path github carrying a five-field GH_TOKEN brief and (2) an unbriefed proposal at brief-requirements, then calls run_steward (which calls steward::run). It asserts that the run returns Ok, the commit holds both items, report.applied is empty, the github item has key blind-spot:github:owner-action, kind Proposal and brief Some, the other has brief None, work_decisions::open_proposals returns only the github item, and athena.status().work_proposals has one entry. Another case first runs a plain github blind spot, then the briefed one, and asserts the briefed one is recorded. xtask: a page test with a briefed in-limit item, a briefed above-limit item, an unbriefed above-limit item and an unbriefed in-limit item shows exactly the two briefed cards.
demonstrations.observes: The briefed item is recorded as Proposed with its brief at any rung, the run succeeds and commits, it is the only open proposal, and no request job is queued for it. The decisions page lists exactly the briefed open proposals.
demonstrations.fails_without: The base decide() applies the Implementation-rung change and drops its brief, so the brief assertion and report.applied.is_empty() fail. The base validate_items uses the brief-ignoring blind_spot_change, so the key and brief assertions fail. An empty-evidence constructor would make run() return Err and the end-to-end test fail. With the base needs_owner the briefed in-limit card is missing from the page.

demonstrations.observes: decide() branches on change.brief.is_some() before role.may_change. open_proposals keeps brief.is_some() || in_limit. in_limit requires brief.is_none(). blind_spot_needing_owner carries a brief, evidence and the :owner-action key, and validate_items calls it when a blind-spot item has a brief. needs_owner in xtask is item.brief.is_some().
